quest.title: Life Flows On (II)
quest.description: After having helped Endora for this period of time, you are finally ready to cut to the heart of this problem.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x60, Endora x1, Mora x30000

talks.objective: Complete the "Rhodeia's Rage" challenge once (after completing it, return to Single-Player Mode to continue the quest)

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: Life flows on...

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: I have reached an understanding with Rhodeia.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: She is the most renowned of us Lochfolk scouts, and also the strongest. But she fled Fontaine, harboring a longing for the previous Hydro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: I can no longer return to Fontaine myself, so let me tell you everything.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: We Lochfolk once spread far and wide to rivers, streams, and ponds all over the continent, and we largely served as Fontaine's spies.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Spies!? What's the Hydro Archon planning?

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: The previous Archon had no plan to speak of. She merely wished to connect everyone in the world, in much the same way as all water is connected. But with her passing, many of us have cut off ties with Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: Like Rhodeia, the strongest of our number, they did not recognize the new Hydro Archon and desired only to keep the dreams of yesteryear alive. All Rhodeia wants is a small haven of tranquil waters.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: But she sensed my presence and believed me to be an assassin from Fontaine, and so she stretched forth her enmity, which turned the water bitter, in order to slay me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you were so small and weak when we first met. Did she really have to put in that much effort?

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: The dominant mind of the Lochfolk can be very easily shattered if we come into contact with another smaller but wicked mind.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: I admired Rhodeia a great deal, and so I piggybacked off a Hydro Slime and left Fontaine, jumping from water body to water body until I finally ended up here.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: I doubt that any other Lochfolk would have shared my level of determination — unless, of course, they were an assassin on a mission.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When you put it like that, it makes you sound pretty awesome...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Still, you can't beat Paimon, who's piggybacking on {NICKNAME}'s journey all over the seven nations and doing just fine so far!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh, come off it, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: I have explained everything to her. The bitterness in the water should dissipate soon. She even asked if I wanted to join together with the waters of Qingce.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So are you here to say goodbye?

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: I still have one message to deliver. Please, accompany me to Springvale once more.

talks.objective: Speak to Old Finch in Springvale

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: Finch, Finch!

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: Oh! You scared me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's not surprised that you're surprised. Endora learns lightning quick, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: No, it's just that... The way you called my name, it sounded just like her...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: "With each small step a child takes, a journey through the world it makes. Drops of knowledge this creates, each one the child assimilates."

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: "Day by day, a child will age. Drop by drop, a life is made."

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: I know this poem.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: Our lives and yours are very different. As such, we may never understand each other, even for so long as we may live.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: But our lives are also the same. We all flow towards the ocean, experiencing new things and encountering new opportunities along the way.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: Thus, she says this: "When the stars in the night sky have all gone out, and all streams and dreams have mingled in the same great ocean... Then, we will meet again."

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: ...I see.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: Life flows on, so please, begin to move again. Do not stand still.

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: Haha, that's her, alright. Still treating me like a kid, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: Alright then. I'd like a quiet moment to myself, if you would.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}, guess we should head back and report to Connor, too.

talks.objective: Go to Dawn Winery and speak to Connor

dialogues.speaker: Connor
dialogues.text: Oh, you're here.

dialogues.speaker: Connor
dialogues.text: I'm guessing that since it was you on the case, everything's been resolved and that's the end of it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The bitter water should be back to normal in a couple o' days.

response.speaker: Connor
response.text: I see, I see. It makes sense — even if you've removed the cause of the problem, it will still take some time for the water to cleanse itself.

response.speaker: Connor
response.text: Well, I suppose I should inform the Adventurers' Guild that this case has been closed.

choices.text: There were some twists and turns...

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: Our kind expresses love by merging water bodies together. This way, many minds can coexist without division.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: But understanding other life-forms in this world is not quite so simple. So we observe, study, imitate, and manifest in the form of animals. You could also say that their forms have become a part of us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like watching the river flow away has caused some deep thoughts to well up in Endora, huh.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: I've never considered how I should live my life after this point. I always assumed that I would merge with Rhodeia, and that this would be good and right.

dialogues.speaker: Endora
dialogues.text: But Rhodeia seemed unhappy. She, too, understands that she is only waiting for pure waters to become corrupted.

response.speaker: Endora
response.text: Neither Rhodeia nor the one who dwells in Springvale wanted me to follow their paths. But surely they must have hated their lives in Fontaine still more.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You guys are fascinating. Paimon's not sure what to say in this situation... But it's probably best to live in a way that makes you happy!

response.speaker: Endora
response.text: I've decided to embark on a path that no others before me have. Journeying with you has been a joyful experience, and I wish for all my future days to be just as joyful.

response.speaker: Endora
response.text: I wish to travel with you. Before this tiny stream of life flows into the ocean, I wish to see everything from the flowers that bloom on its banks to the clouds that sit on the horizon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wait a minute, {NICKNAME}... Does this mean that the position of transcontinental travel companion is no longer a Paimon-only privilege?

choices.text: Is that why you refused her?

dialogues.speaker: Connor
dialogues.text: You know, we did have a last-resort solution, which was to use the water of Springvale to make wine. I'm sure Draff would have agreed — goodness knows what he'd do without wine, after all.
